seoTitle: Serengeti National Park — Complete Safari Guide 2026
intro: Serengeti National Park is Tanzania's most iconic wildlife destination and a UNESCO World Heritage Site covering 14,763 square kilometres of open savanna, woodland, and riverine forest in the Mara Region. Home to the greatest wildlife spectacle on earth — the annual Great Wildebeest Migration — the Serengeti supports over 70 large mammal species and 500 bird species in one of Africa's last intact savanna ecosystems.

sections.heading: The Great Wildebeest Migration
sections.content: Each year, over 1.5 million wildebeest, 200,000 zebra, and 300,000 Thomson's gazelle complete a 1,200-kilometre circular migration through the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem. The cycle follows seasonal rains: calving on the southern plains (January–February), the push north through the western corridor (May–June), dramatic Mara River crossings in the north (July–October), and the return south (November–December). The river crossings — where crocodiles ambush thousands of wildebeest simultaneously — are the most photographed wildlife event in the world.

sections.heading: Big Five and Predator Density
sections.content: The Serengeti holds approximately 3,000 lion in multiple prides — one of Africa's highest densities. Leopard are reliably spotted in kopjes (granite outcrops) near Seronera. Cheetah hunt on the open southern plains. The park has healthy elephant and buffalo populations year-round. Black rhino numbers are small but present in the western corridor. Spotted hyena are abundant; African wild dog packs — one of Africa's most endangered carnivores — are occasionally sighted in the north.

sections.heading: Best Areas Within the Serengeti
sections.content: The Seronera Valley (central) offers year-round predator action around permanent water. The southern plains (Ndutu area) are best January–March for calving and concentrations. The western corridor is prime for Migration in May–June with Grumeti River crossings. The northern Kogatende sector, near the Kenyan border, hosts the Mara River crossings July–October — the most dramatic Migration phase, but accessible mainly by fly-in. The remote Loliondo area adjoining the park offers exclusive walking safaris and night drives not permitted inside.

sections.heading: Practical Safari Information
sections.content: Entry fees: $70/person/day plus $70/vehicle/day. Most visits are 3–5 days minimum. Accommodation ranges from public campsites ($35/night) to ultra-luxury mobile camps ($800–1,500/person/night). The park is accessible by road from Arusha via Ngorongoro (6–8 hours) or by scheduled charter flights to Seronera, Kogatende, or Grumeti airstrips. Self-drive is permitted with a 4x4. Guides significantly improve wildlife spotting — they know predator territories and current Migration positions. Book accommodation and flights 6–12 months ahead for July–September.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Serengeti National Park?
faqs.a: It depends on what you want to see. July–October for Mara River crossings (Migration peak). January–February for calving season and predator action. June–October for the dry season with best general game viewing. The park is excellent year-round.

faqs.q: How do I get to Serengeti National Park from Arusha?
faqs.a: By road: 6–8 hours via Ngorongoro Conservation Area in a 4x4 — most safari vehicles use this route. By air: 45–60 minutes on a scheduled charter flight from Arusha's Kilimanjaro airport to Seronera airstrip. Fly-in is strongly recommended for the remote northern sector.

faqs.q: Can I see the Big Five in the Serengeti?
faqs.a: Yes — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and black rhino are all present. Lion and leopard are reliably sighted near Seronera. Rhino are rarer and mostly in the western corridor. A 3-day central Serengeti safari typically produces 4 of the 5.

faqs.q: Is the Serengeti worth the high cost?
faqs.a: For most visitors who experience it, yes. The park fees and accommodation costs are high but the wildlife density and landscapes are unmatched in Africa. Budget travellers can reduce costs by using public campsites, self-driving, and visiting in the shoulder season (March–May or November).

tips: Book Kogatende camps 6–12 months ahead for July–September river crossings
Early morning game drives (06:00) produce the most predator activity
A balloon safari over the Serengeti at dawn is expensive but extraordinary
The central Seronera area is the most accessible and productive year-round base
Bring a long telephoto lens — plains animals are often distant from the vehicle
